sentences.text: Leaellynasaura was a small, slender, herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur that lived in Australia.
Recent estimates suggest the body length was roughly 180 centimeters, though other analyses estimate the total length including the tail could reach up to 3 meters.
A skull fragment shows an enlarged eye socket and large optic lobes, suggesting an adaptation to low-light conditions.
The species was first discovered in the Eumeralla Formation at Dinosaur Cove, Australia.
The genus was named by Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich in 1989 after their daughter, Leaellyn Rich.
There are four recorded fossil occurrences of this animal known to science.
Dietary analysis indicates it ate low-growing plants such as horsetails, cycads, and ferns.
Herne argued that Leaellynasaura lacked ossified tendons in its tail, a feature found in more advanced ornithischians.
It is debated whether the large eyes were an adaptation to low-light conditions or simply characteristic of a juvenile individual.
Leaellynasaura is classified in the class Ornithischia.
A 2019 study recovered the animal as a member of the clade Elasmaria.
Leaellynasaura lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, specifically from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
During this time, the province of Victoria, Australia, was located within the Antarctic Circle.
